lists.title: Metals
lists.note: International benchmarks from Yahoo, not MCX. NSE publishes no commodity data and MCX refuses automated access. These track the rupee contracts but are a different instrument, currency and contract size.

items.label: Gold
items.channel: Read here as a risk-off confirmation rather than as a commodity: when gold is bid alongside the dollar, the tape is hedging rather than rotating. It is also a live import-bill line, and the gold-loan books mark against it.

items.label: Copper
items.channel: Realisation for the integrated producers, and the standing proxy for global industrial demand. Reaches NIFTY METAL properly and the broad index only faintly -- it is four large stocks, not the market.

items.label: Iron ore 62%
items.channel: Steel realisation against input cost. Positive for the integrated miners and negative for the converters, so the index effect is smaller than the sector noise suggests.

lists.title: Energy
lists.note: International benchmarks from Yahoo, not MCX. NSE publishes no commodity data and MCX refuses automated access. These track the rupee contracts but are a different instrument, currency and contract size.

items.label: Brent
items.channel: India imports about 88% of the crude it burns and pays for it in dollars. Roughly $10/bbl is 0.3-0.4pp on headline CPI and around $14bn on the current account, which is why this channel reaches the rate path and not only the oil names.

items.label: Crude WTI
items.channel: The same channel as Brent and largely the same information. Weighted low on purpose: India prices its basket off Brent and Dubai, so counting WTI at full weight would double-count one move.

items.label: Coal API2
items.channel: Imported thermal coal, which sets the marginal cost of power and the input cost of every converter. Small weight because most Indian generation burns domestic coal at a regulated price.

items.label: Nat Gas
items.channel: City-gas input cost. The pass-through is regulated and lagged, so a move lands on margin well before it lands on the consumer.

lists.title: Agri & softs
lists.note: International benchmarks from Yahoo, not MCX. NSE publishes no commodity data and MCX refuses automated access. These track the rupee contracts but are a different instrument, currency and contract size.

items.label: Sugar #11
items.channel: Sector-local rather than index-level, and policy dominates it: the export quota decides the domestic price far more than the world price does.

items.label: Soybean oil
items.channel: Standing in for crude palm oil, India's largest edible-oil import, which has no free feed. Moves FMCG gross margin within a quarter and shows up in food CPI before that.

items.label: Wheat
items.channel: Food is roughly 46% of the CPI basket. A sustained move here is the fastest route there is from a commodity screen to a rate decision.

lists.title: FX & rates
lists.note: International benchmarks from Yahoo, not MCX. NSE publishes no commodity data and MCX refuses automated access. These track the rupee contracts but are a different instrument, currency and contract size.

items.label: Dollar index
items.channel: The one driver that splits the index. A bid dollar pulls FPI money out of cash equity, which is negative for NIFTY -- and is simultaneously positive for the exporters inside it, because IT and pharma bill in dollars and pay costs in rupees. Read the index effect and the sector effect as two separate facts, not as a contradiction.

items.label: USD/INR
items.channel: The rupee itself, which does not always follow the dollar index -- RBI intervention and importer demand move it on their own. Weighted below the dollar index because the two overlap, and kept separate because when they disagree the disagreement is the signal.

items.label: US 10-year
items.channel: The discount rate on long-duration India. It compresses the multiple the market will pay before it touches a single earnings estimate, which is why it hits the expensive end of the market hardest. Note ref is 2% OF THE YIELD, so about 10bp on a 5% handle -- not 2 percentage points.

items.label: VIX
items.channel: Global risk appetite in one number. It is not an India channel in itself -- it is the channel through which every other risk asset gets sold at once, and India VIX follows it with a lag more often than it leads.
